runs.name: the-ledger-keeps-the-failures
runs.title: The ledger keeps the failures
runs.summary:
Reviewed the verification ledger from newest to oldest, covering 16 runs: 7 passed and 9 failed.
The runs were: The ledger keeps the failures (failed); The app refuses a program that does not fit (passed, then four failed runs); The staircase can be walked to (passed, then two failed runs); Nothing stands in a doorway (passed); Every room can be walked to (passed, then failed); Every room has a door (passed); The app opens on a drawn plan (passed); audit-plan-walkability (passed, then failed).
Each listed run showed its status, the commit it was checked against, the app’s own checker findings, and its individual flow results; failed runs remained visibly marked as failed.
Assertion results: passed—plot-size validation and plan regeneration; staircase review; doorway-blocking-furniture review; room-access review; floor-plan findings and status review; drawn-plan review; and one audit-plan-walkability room-access review.
Assertion results: failed—the ledger review was not shown as complete; four plot-size checks stopped early or lacked required area details; two staircase checks found the upper-floor arrival missing or incorrectly treated the stairwell door as absent; one room-access check stopped before reporting; and the failed audit identified inaccessible Bedroom 3, Bathroom 2, Bedroom 1, Bedroom 2, Bathroom 1, an unusable and undersized hall, no staircase door, furniture blocking doorways (sofa, counter, and bed), and a missing required drawing detail. Overall, 7 of 27 recorded assertions passed and 20 failed.

The plan was healthy: the Ground floor view showed a door into the stairwell and a route from the front door, the findings panel showed no problems, and the Floor 2 view showed the stair. After checking each floor, record the observations separately and finish: the stair has a door, the findings panel says “Nothing found,” it appears on both storeys, and it is usable.

runs.name: the-ledger-keeps-the-failures
runs.title: The ledger keeps the failures
runs.summary:
The agent opened the Ledger but did not complete a run-by-run review from newest to oldest before making the assertion. The visible ledger was scrollable and only part of the list was examined, so the test could not establish that every entry included both a commit and the app's findings.
Update the automation to scroll through the entire Ledger, expand or read each run as needed, record its status, commit, checker report, and individual flow outcomes, and only then evaluate the completeness assertions.

runs.title: The app refuses a program that does not fit
runs.summary:
The agent became stuck after extracting the refusal details and repeatedly waited instead of completing the remaining required reporting steps. Update the workflow to save the refusal text immediately, then explicitly set the plot back to 18 by 14, generate, verify the returned drawing, and produce the requested assertion summary instead of issuing repeated waits.
